sample_unit: complex rheumatologic case vignettes (each evaluated at 3 time points per model)

links.outcome: Correlation between LLM reasoning quality and expressed certainty (calibration)
links.effect: Weak, non-significant associations between reasoning quality and expressed certainty across all models (rho range -0.156 to 0.215, all p>0.05), indicating miscalibration.
links.quote: However, Spearman correlation analysis revealed uniformly weak and non-significant associations between reasoning quality and expressed certainty across all models (ρ range: -0.156 to 0.215, all p>0.05), indicating fundamental miscalibration.

links.outcome: Temporal stability/reproducibility of LLM outputs across repeated runs at Days 1, 5, 10
links.effect: Temporal stability was excellent for ChatGPT (ICC=0.84) and good for DeepSeek (ICC=0.79).
links.quote: Temporal stability was excellent for ChatGPT (ICC=0.84) and good for DeepSeek (ICC=0.79).

links.outcome: Hallucination frequency of LLMs on rheumatology cases
links.effect: ChatGPT lowest hallucination rate (7.4%); Gemini highest (18.5%).
links.quote: ChatGPT demonstrated the highest reasoning score (3.89±0.23) and lowest hallucination rate (7.4%), while Gemini showed the highest hallucination frequency (18.5%).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the performance, reasoning quality, calibration, temporal stability, and hallucination rates of four LLMs using published complex rheumatology case vignettes without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
